n. (Strange)人名；(英)斯特兰奇；(瑞典、塞)斯特朗格
短语：feel strange — 感到不舒服
短语：strange to say — 说来奇怪
短语：look strange — ◎显得奇怪，显得不寻常
短语：make strange — [主方言]表现得不友好，表现得令人吃惊
短语：strange attractor — 奇异吸引体
例句：strange noises
奇怪的噪声
例句：Does Geoff’s behaviour seem strange to you?
你觉得杰夫的行为反常吗？
例句：She felt there was something strange about Dexter’s voice.
她觉得德克斯特的声音有点奇怪。
例句：Isn’t it strange how animals seem to sense danger?
动物似乎能感觉到危险，这不是很奇怪吗？
例句：It’s strange that we’ve never met before.
很奇怪，我们以前居然从来没有碰见过。
例句：For some strange reason, I slept like a baby despite the noise.
很奇怪，不知为什么，尽管很吵闹，但我仍睡得很香。
例句：Strange as it may seem, I actually prefer cold weather.
听上去也许很奇怪，我竟然喜欢冷天。
例句：That’s strange. I was sure Jude was right here a second ago.
真奇怪，我肯定祖德刚刚还在这儿的。
例句：The strange thing is all four victims had red hair.
令人奇怪的是，四名受害者都是红头发的。

例句：Our friendship has steadily strengthened over the years.

例句：Steve’s opposition only strengthened her resolve to go ahead.

例句：The company plans to strengthen its hand (= make itself more powerful ) in Europe by opening an office in Spain.
